description: §14.8.9 — the explicit null-body form `new Response(not, { status: 302, headers: { Location: ... } })` in a `protect=` file compiles with NO protect diagnostic at all: not E-PROTECT-005 (it carries no body) and not W-PROTECT-005 (the runtime guard recognizes it exactly via `.body === null` and passes it through with its status and headers intact). This is the resolution W-PROTECT-005 names, so it is pinned as a case rather than asserted in prose.
rationale: A diagnostic that names a working path owes a proof that the path works. W-PROTECT-005 tells the adopter to write this exact shape, so this case compiles it: `not` (scrml's absence, §42) lowers to a JS `null` body, which is the one thing both the compile scan (`isProvablyNullBodyResponse`) and the runtime guard (`.body === null`) recognize as payload-free. Together with `w-protect-005-null-body-static` this pins the adopter-facing contract of the §14.8.9 floor: a `protect=` app keeps full control of STATUS and HEADERS; what it gives up is authoring the BODY.
